record.original_question: Is there an algorithm deciding if a given one-relator group is hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: Is there an algorithm deciding if a given one-relator group is hyperbolic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finitely presented group $G = \langle X \mid r \rangle$ given by a finite alphabet $X$ together with a single relator $r$ (a freely reduced word in $X \cup X^{-1}$) is called a one-relator group. A finitely generated group is called (Gromov) hyperbolic if its Cayley graph (with respect to some, equivalently any, finite generating set) is a $\delta$-hyperbolic geodesic metric space for some $\delta \geq 0$; equivalently, every geodesic triangle in the Cayley graph is $\delta$-thin.

Decide: does there exist an algorithm which, on input a finite presentation $\langle X \mid r \rangle$ of a one-relator group $G$, halts and outputs "yes" if $G$ is hyperbolic and "no" otherwise?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of algorithmically deciding hyperbolicity of one-relator groups is widely cited as open. While one-relator groups with torsion are known to be hyperbolic, and there are conjectural characterizations (e.g., a one-relator group is hyperbolic iff it contains no Baumslag–Solitar subgroup), no complete decision algorithm is known in general. Only partial/semi-algorithms exist (e.g., for free-by-cyclic groups).

status_evidence.title: One-Relator Groups II: Hyperbolicity and Torsion
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 39 is to determine which one-relator groups are hyperbolic... Although Problem 39 is wide open, some answers have been conjectured. Conjecture 40: a one-relator group is hyperbolic iff it contains no Baumslag–Solitar subgroup.
status_evidence.claim: The classification/decidability of hyperbolicity among one-relator groups is described as wide open.

status_evidence.title: Encoding and Detecting Properties in Finitely Presented Groups (Gardam)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of partial algorithms for hyperbolicity and the difficulty of deciding hyperbolicity for general finitely presented groups including one-relator groups.
status_evidence.claim: No complete algorithm is known to decide hyperbolicity of one-relator groups.
